subject: Critical Thinking
title: In-Group Bias: Us vs. Them
description: One-minute skill: In-Group Bias: Us vs. Them.

hook.text: Henri Tajfel assigned people to groups by coin flip.

buildup.text: In-group bias: we favor members of our own group — even when the group is arbitrary and meaningless.

discovery.text: This bias operates on every axis: nationality, religion, sports teams, even which brand of phone you use.

twist.text: In-group bias doesn't require hating the out-group. It just requires giving your group the benefit of the doubt.

climax.text: It's the foundation of tribalism, nationalism, and partisan politics — and it activates in milliseconds.

punchline.text: You don't need a reason to favor your group. You do it by default.

quiz.question: What did Tajfel's experiments show about group identity?
options: Group favoritism requires a meaningful reason
People favor their group even when it's randomly assigned

details.summary: In-group bias makes you favor people who belong to your group and distrust outsiders, even when groups are formed randomly. This tribal instinct shapes politics, hiring, and interpersonal trust.
details.whyItMatters: In-group bias fuels discrimination, political polarization, and workplace favoritism. Recognizing it is the first step toward fairer judgment.
takeaways: Even arbitrary group membership creates in-group favoritism
Minimal group experiments show how little it takes to trigger bias
Cross-group contact and shared goals reduce the effect

faq.question: How does in-group bias affect hiring decisions in the workplace?
faq.answer: Interviewers tend to favor candidates who share their background, school, or interests. Structured interviews with standardized criteria reduce this bias by focusing evaluation on job-relevant skills.

faq.question: Can in-group bias be completely eliminated through awareness?
faq.answer: Awareness helps but does not eliminate it. Structural changes like blind review processes, diverse interview panels, and objective scoring rubrics are more effective than individual effort alone.
